To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the average Turkish securities firm was found to be 60.5% efficient; (2) foreign owned and affiliated firms were found to be the most efficient, while local and unaffiliated firms were the least efficient; (3) size and the degree of foreign ownership had a positive effect on efficiency; (4) the liabilities of foreignness and localness were found to be significant in determining the efficiency of securities firm; and, (5) the liability of market globalness
the securities firms in Turkey are not efficient in the use of their inputs.
The size of securities firms in the Turkish securities industry has a positive and significant impact on their efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of securities firms in a globalised emerging market economy and is the first study to examine the efficiency of securities industry in Turkey.
the impact of the LOF and LOL on the efficiency of knowledge intensive firms.
the impact of LOF, LOL and LOMG upon the efficiency of securities trading firms in an emerging economy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficiency of securities firm is affected by size, bank affiliation and foreign owned securities firm.

the efficiency of Turkish securities firms can be explained by the following factors: (1) the level of foreign ownership of the securities firm; (2) the size of the firm; (3) the extent of bank ownership; (4) the degree of market globalness; (5) the extent of the firm’s localness.
the securities firms of Turkey are not efficient in terms of their use of inputs to generate output.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our study provides a useful benchmarking tool to help securities firms improve efficiency in a globalised environment.
we provide a novel approach to the analysis of emerging market securities firms and offer insights into how these firms might be managed more effectively in the future.
the securities firm industry in Turkey is characterized by the presence of foreign firms, which is a result of the country’s economic liberalisation policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emerging economies are not homogenous and that the LOF, LOMG and LOL are important in determining the performance of firms in such markets.
foreign owned securities firms are more efficient than their local counterparts.
emerging markets can be an attractive market for foreign firms.
